\chapter{A Package Abroad}
\label{ch:paquete-extranjero}
\hlchaptermodality{415}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can identify a package being sent abroad in a simple post-office message.}

Retrieve package and abroad in a short post-office instruction.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[el paquete]{el paquete — a bundle packed for travel}

\label{lesson:ES-C415-paquete}



\begin{quote}
Recall \textbf{el impreso}, the form you fill in. At a post office, the form may travel with \textbf{el paquete}, the package or parcel.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
Spanish borrowed \textbf{paquete} through French \textbf{paquet}, a small bundle. English \textbf{packet} travelled from the same word, and \textbf{pack} is a close family clue. Picture several things packed together into one parcel.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: what happens to the package?}]
The noun is masculine: \textbf{el paquete}, \textbf{un paquete}. Use \textbf{enviar} for the action: \textbf{enviar el paquete}, to send the package.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{el paquete}
  \item \emph{un paquete}
  \item \emph{enviar el paquete}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Package? (\emph{El paquete}.) To send the package? (\emph{Enviar el paquete}.)

Source: \href{https://dle.rae.es/paquete}{DLE: paquete}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[el extranjero]{el extranjero — the world outside one's country}

\label{lesson:ES-C415-extranjero}



\begin{quote}
Recall \textbf{el paquete}. If it crosses a national border, you can send it \textbf{al extranjero}, abroad.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
The family reaches back to Latin \textbf{extraneus}, “from outside.” It travelled through Romance in several directions; English \textbf{strange} and \textbf{stranger} are distant relatives. Spanish \textbf{extranjero} can name a foreign person, but \textbf{el extranjero} in the frame \textbf{al extranjero} means abroad.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: a + el}]
Spanish contracts \textbf{a + el} to \textbf{al}: \textbf{enviar el paquete al extranjero}. The place frame, not a person's nationality, is the useful meaning here.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{el extranjero}
  \item \emph{al extranjero}
  \item \emph{enviar el paquete al extranjero}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Abroad? (\emph{Al extranjero}.)

Source: \href{https://dle.rae.es/extranjero}{DLE: extranjero}.
\end{tcolorbox}
